description: Research: best open handheld gripper system released in 2026 only. Jake (voice): 'It looks like this Grabette is kind of along the right lines. Is this most likely to be the best one? Again, we should look for things that are done in 2026 specifically.' Sweep 2026 releases only (papers, repos, kits), with Grabette (Pollen/HF, July 2026, Apache-2.0) as the baseline, plus UMI-3D and anything newer. Compare: license and what's actually released (CAD/STL/BOM/code), matching robot-side gripper, tracking method and cost, LeRobot export, fit for our SO-101 arms and Gen 6-8 designs. Give a clear verdict on whether Grabette is the one to build on, and update plans/handheld_gripper.md (it currently marks Grabette's license unverified; it's Apache-2.0).

results.identified_issue: Sources: GitHub API license field (Apache-2.0, repo created 2026-06-08, pushed 2026-10-15); HF blog 2026-07-21 (490€/120€ BOM, RTAB-Map, OAK-D SR + fisheye, 200-demo DP on OpenArm, no metrics); docs/source/gripette.md (2x STS3215, Pi Zero 2W, gRPC ~10Hz camera). YUBI: yubi.airoa.io + toyota/yubi-hw README (CERN-OHL-W v2, Dynamixel, Franka/OpenArm/G1 flanges, Quest 3S tracking, dataset coming soon). HiFi-UMI/PolyUMI from arXiv abstracts only — no repo/license found, may exist on project pages. Unverified: Gripette mass; whether Gripette's STS3215s share the SO-101's bus IDs/baud; PolyUMI affiliations. Search was via web summaries, so a 2026 release could be missing (I checked YUBI, HiFi-UMI, PolyUMI, UMI-3D, YAM-UMI, UMI-LINGO). The previous plan said adapt Hand 1.0; this reverses the hardware choice only, the method stays. Gripette's camera conflicts with the head-stereo principle; flagged, not resolved.
results.summary: Yes — among 2026 releases, Grabette is the one to build on; its robot gripper even runs on the SO-101's own servo.
results.detailed_description:
I looked at every open handheld gripper released in 2026. Grabette wins for us: it's Apache-2.0 with CAD, STL, BOM and code all published, it exports straight to LeRobot, and it costs about 490 € for the handheld plus 120 € for the robot side. Its robot gripper (Gripette) uses two Feetech STS3215s, the same servo as the SO-101. The strongest rival is Toyota's YUBI (June). It has better evidence and an 8,000-hour dataset on the way, but it uses Dynamixel servos and a Quest 3S, and it's built for Franka-sized arms. UMI-3D needs LiDAR and ROS, HiFi-UMI released only a dataset, and PolyUMI is a tactile research rig.

Grabette doesn't give us everything. There's no SO-101 integration yet (only OpenArm), so we'd write the wrist mount and the 5-DOF retargeting ourselves. Gripette's weight isn't published, so it needs weighing against the SO-101 wrist limit. Its evidence is also thin: one cup task with no success numbers.

I updated plans/handheld_gripper.md: its license is now Apache-2.0, there's a new §1a with the 2026 comparison and verdict, and the pilot now builds one Grabette + Gripette instead of the Hand 1.0 + iPhone clip-on. Next step if you agree: order Pollen's BOM and weigh Gripette.
results.user_reply_draft: Hey Jake — good instinct. Grabette holds up as the best open handheld gripper from 2026 to build on. It's fully open, it plugs into LeRobot, and its robot-side gripper uses the same servo as our SO-101 arms. Toyota's YUBI is the one to watch for its dataset, but its hardware doesn't fit our arms. I've written up the comparison and updated the plan. Next step is ordering Grabette's parts and weighing the robot gripper.

summary: Jake wants a sweep of 2026-only open handheld gripper systems, comparing Grabette (Apache-2.0) against UMI-3D and newer releases. Give a clear verdict on building on Grabette for SO-101 and Gen 6-8, and update plans/handheld_gripper.md.
